transcript.text: Indesit washer dryer washes fine but the drying cycle doesn't get warm at all, clothes come out cold and wet after 2 hours. Model is XWDE 96 something.

Clothes that are still cold after two hours point more towards the drying heat not being produced than simply a large load. The main possibilities are a fault in the drying heater circuit (heater, thermal cut-out or thermostat), a drying setting issue, or less commonly the cold-water supply used for condensation being off or restricted. Try a small, well-spun load on a timed dry for 15–20 minutes, with the cold tap fully open and hose untwisted; there is no need to dismantle anything. If it remains completely cold, it is likely to need an engineer to test the internal drying heater circuit and controls safely.

I haven't tried the small load yet, but the door glass is stone cold when it's drying, and the cold tap is on. There's no burning smell and nothing trips. Is there anything else I should check before calling an engineer?

There is one useful check before arranging a visit: establish whether the wash is completing a proper final spin. If laundry is coming out dripping wet, the dryer is starting with far too much water and the fault may be in spinning/draining rather than the dryer itself. If it is normally spun and only damp, a stone-cold door throughout a two-hour dry makes an internal drying-heater circuit fault the leading cause—typically the heater, thermal cut-out/thermostat or its control. Those parts need internal electrical testing, so an engineer is the sensible next step rather than dismantling it.

The clothes come out of the spin normally, just damp not dripping. It stopped heating after I unplugged it mid-dry last week to grab a shirt, if that matters. I can take the top off if there's something worth looking at.

There is not much worthwhile to inspect with the top off: the likely parts are internal and a visual look would not reliably identify the fault. Keep it unplugged if you do remove the top, but do not touch wiring or try to test anything live. Stopping it by unplugging mid-dry would not normally cause this on its own, although it may have happened around the time a heater circuit component failed. As it spins normally, the cold tap is on, and the door remains stone cold, the drying heater circuit is the leading possibility; airflow restriction more often gives some heat but poor drying. The small timed-dry test is the last useful owner-safe confirmation—if it stays completely cold, arrange an engineer to test the drying heater, thermal protection and control circuit.

candidates: Drying heater circuit fault (heater, thermal cut-out or thermostat) (high)
Drying programme/setting or an overloaded drying load (medium)
